children: The rent freeze backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration has been upheld by a state judge, who dismissed a lawsuit filed by landlords seeking to overturn the measure, which took effect last month.

Landlords filed a lawsuit against the city’s Rent Guidelines Board in July, alleging that Mamdani unduly swayed the vote and that the board disregarded evidence of increasing operating expenses for property owners.
A judge on Wednesday threw out the case, saying the decision to implement the
was not “unreasonable, arbitrary or capricious” and must be upheld.

However, the judge, Brendan T. Lantry, criticized Mamdani’s campaign promises to freeze the rent. “The court recognizes that political candidates routinely comment on prevalent policy issues while running for an elected position,” Lantry wrote in his decision, “but to guarantee a rent freeze to millions of New Yorkers without the authority to do so, is irresponsible.”

Correspondence between the mayor’s office and the board about the measure was “troubling” and “puts a dark shadow over the purported ‘independence’ of the board,” but it doesn’t show that the mayor dictated the decision, Lantry said

In a statement to the New York Times, Mamdani described the decision as “a victory for tenants, for affordability and for the principle that working New Yorkers deserve a city they can afford to live in”. “Because housing is not a luxury,” Mamdani said. “It is a basic necessity.”

The suit came weeks after the board voted for the first time ever to freeze rents for both one-year and two-year leases for roughly 1 million stabilized apartments. The last one-year rent freeze was during the pandemic in 2020. Courts have historically deferred to the Rent Guidelines Board.
Publicly traded real estate companies with exposure to New York City’s rental market include Vivmark Residential
